eval.title: Buffett Stock To Buy = Berkshire - Q3 Earnings Report & Buyback Impact

call.headline_quote: so the answer whether berkshire is a buy or not it is about you not about whether the stock will go up or down

base_metric.name: fcf_per_share
base_metric.quote: you compare this cash flows earnings of 30 billion per year you compare it to the stock price of 500 billion

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: 30 billion divided by 500 billion is 6 that is what you can expect from investing in berkshire now perhaps two percent growth inflation reinvesting we are at eight percent

reasons.claim: Free cash flow of about 30 billion against a 500 billion market cap gives a 6% yield, plus ~2% growth, for roughly 8% expected return.
reasons.quote: 30 billion divided by 500 billion is 6 that is what you can expect from investing in berkshire now perhaps two percent growth inflation reinvesting we are at eight percent

data_check.gap_note: he says 3e+10, as-of 3.8687e+10 (FY2019); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: market cap, cash flow yield, expected return

reasons.claim: Buffett's large and accelerating buybacks (9.3 billion in Q3, plus 2.3 billion in October) confirm he believes Berkshire is undervalued.
reasons.quote: warren buffett spent 9.3 billion on buybacks which is almost double what we he spent in q2 and much more than what he usually spent on berkshire buybacks

data_check.gap_note: he says 2.3e+09, as-of -4.85e+09 (FY2019); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: Q3 buybacks

reasons.claim: Because Berkshire's shares are heavily held by long-term index funds and Buffett himself, the stock is inelastic to supply, so large buybacks push the price higher.
reasons.quote: because berkshire is heavily owned by funds mutual funds just vanguard blackrock and others own 20 20 something percent of berkshire other funds plus warren buffett owns 30 something so berkshire is a very inelastic stock

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: fund ownership, Buffett ownership

reasons.claim: Operating profits are still strong despite the covid recession and should rise further once the economy recovers.
reasons.quote: operating profits are strong and high at around 5 billion when the recession passes when there is again economic growth this will again go higher higher and higher

data_check.gap_note: he says 5e+09, as-of 8.1417e+10 (FY2019); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Buffett will slow buybacks once the stock is fairly valued, which limits further upside from that source and signals the price level to watch.
reasons.quote: he is really pushing on buybacks and we'll see when will he stop because when he stops it will mean that berkshire is let's say fairly valued

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated
